children.text: Conventional intramedullary osteosarcomas are malignant, aggressive, osteogenic bone tumors most commonly found in the knee and shoulder regions. Patients are typically children, teenagers or young adults who present with rapidly progressive pain and swelling.
Diagnosis is made with a biopsy showing malignant-appearing mesenchymal spindle cells with significant atypia, pleomorphism and mitotic figures producing lace-like woven bone (osteoid).
Treatment is usually neo-adjuvant chemotherapy, limb sparing surgery (wide surgical resection and reconstruction), followed by adjuvant chemotherapy. Amputation may occasionally be required.
